items.title: Depart Syracuse (SYR) — Regional connection to New York (JFK)
items.notes: SYR → JFK Terminal 4 · Regional connection · arrive 7:03am · Economy. Keep passport & onward boarding passes handy
items.location: Syracuse Hancock Intl (SYR) → New York JFK (T4)

items.title: Layover at New York (JFK) Terminal 4
items.notes: Connection to the long-haul, same terminal. Under three hours with the 15-hour leg on the other side of it, so eat before boarding rather than after clearing the gate

items.title: Fly JFK → Delhi (DEL) — Long-haul to Delhi
items.notes: JFK T4 → DEL Terminal 3 · Long-haul to Delhi · arrives 11:40am Dec 10 · Economy. Long-haul — set watch ahead, hydrate, sleep on board

items.title: Layover at Delhi (DEL) Terminal 3
items.notes: Same-terminal international connection at Indira Gandhi Intl before the final hop to Kathmandu — enough time for the transfer-security queue

items.title: Fly Delhi (DEL) → Kathmandu (KTM) — Delhi → Kathmandu
items.notes: DEL T3 → KTM Terminal I · Delhi → Kathmandu · arrives 4:10pm · Economy. Window seat for first glimpses of the Himalaya on descent

items.title: Arrive Tribhuvan (KTM): visa on arrival & transfer
items.notes: Visa on arrival, baggage claim, currency exchange to Nepali rupees, then transfer into the city

items.title: Check in to the Thamel hotel
items.notes: 3-star hotel in Thamel, beside the Garden of Dreams and a short walk from the old town; rest and freshen up after the long journey

items.title: Evening walk in Thamel
items.notes: Ease into the city — buy a local SIM card, browse the shops, get oriented

items.title: Welcome dinner at Bhojan Griha
items.notes: Traditional Nepali dal bhat feast in a 150-year-old heritage building with a cultural dance show — reserve ahead

items.title: Transfer to Tribhuvan's DOMESTIC terminal
items.notes: The mountain flight goes from the domestic terminal, about 600 m north of the international terminal you landed at. Do not navigate to a generic KTM pin — it lands mid-airfield

items.title: Everest Experience mountain flight
items.notes: An hour at around 25,000 ft: every seat is a window seat and the plane turns so both sides get the same view — the one thing that beats the December haze outright. Booked early in the stay on purpose, because winter radiation fog has closed Tribhuvan outright and a cancellation gets rescheduled, so this must not be left to the 18th. Book direct at buddhaair.com or through the hotel

items.title: Breakfast at Pumpernickel Bakery
items.notes: Open from 06:30, the only Thamel cafe confirmed to serve before 07:00. The walled garden is cold until about 09:00 in December — start indoors and move out when the sun reaches the courtyard

items.title: Drive to Kirtipur
items.notes: 15-30 minutes by taxi at about NPR 450-700; the local bus from just south of Ratna Park is about NPR 35 and takes 25 minutes

items.title: Nepal v India 'A' T20I at the TU International Cricket Ground
items.notes: A day game, not floodlit — gates open 60-90 minutes before the 10:00 start and a T20 finishes around 13:15. Confirm the fixture with the Cricket Association of Nepal nearer the time; tickets are Khalti-only, so the hotel may need to buy them. No re-entry, so bring water

items.title: Kirtipur old town & Uma Maheshwor hill
items.notes: A 15-minute walk uphill from the ground on uneven stone, for the old Newar town and the ridge view across to Chandragiri. NPR 100 town entry for non-Nepalis when the ticket booth is staffed, which it frequently is not

items.title: Late lunch at Newa Lahana
items.notes: Community-run Newari khaja ghar at the top of the hill, rice beer brewed on site, open to 21:00 and no reservation needed. Ask for an indoor floor — the top floor is unheated and goes cold fast once the sun drops. Cash is safest

items.title: Live music at Purple Haze Rock Bar
items.notes: Back in Thamel for the first full Kathmandu night — Purple Haze's live rock/blues bands. Thamel bars wind down ~23:00-midnight (loosely enforced); verify hours/cover before going.

items.title: Sunrise at Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple)
items.notes: 365 steps to a 360° valley panorama; sunrise is 06:44-06:49 in mid-December. On the valley floor the haze burns off through the morning and thickens again after lunch, so the city shots want this end of the day

items.title: Boudha Farmers Market in the Utpala Cafe garden
items.notes: Saturday-only, roughly 08:00-14:00 in the monastery cafe's walled garden, with the kitchen switching to a buffet rather than a-la-carte. This is the trip's only Saturday and the reason the Boudha day sits here — worth confirming the market is running that week

items.title: Kopan Monastery viewpoint
items.notes: Hilltop monastery looking down on Boudhanath; prayer flags and golden roofs — respect the quiet hours

items.title: Lunch at Coffee Beans Specialty Coffee, Tushal
items.notes: A bright upstairs shophouse a few minutes off the kora, indoors and warm, open 07:00-20:00. Ask the price of the lot before you pick it — the house filter is about NPR 200 and the 'specialty' lots about NPR 400, and staff do not always volunteer the difference

items.title: Taragaon Next
items.notes: 1970s brick-vaulted modernist complex about 600 m west of the stupa, open daily 10:00-17:30 including Saturday. Assume there is nothing on site to eat or drink, and register ahead through the form on taragaonnext.com if you want the guided tour

items.title: Sunset at Boudhanath Stupa
items.notes: Walk clockwise with the pilgrims and shoot the dome from a rooftop cafe. Sunset is about 17:15, so the golden light is on the whitewash from roughly 16:30 and the butter lamps come after

items.title: Casino Royale
items.notes: Free-entry casino in the Yak & Yeti palace building — table games and slots, open 24/7. Bring a passport; closed-toe shoes required.

items.title: Club Deja Vu
items.notes: Saturday is Kathmandu's best club night — high-capacity dance club a short cab from the casino. Verify hours/cover before going.

items.title: Patan Durbar Square
items.notes: The finest Newari architecture in the valley — the Krishna Temple and the Golden Temple ring the square. Morning is the clean window, before the valley haze thickens again through the afternoon

items.title: Patan Museum
items.notes: The best museum in Nepal — Hindu and Buddhist bronze and stone art, in a restored palace wing on the square itself

items.title: Lunch at Honacha
items.notes: The old Newari bhatti in the alley behind Krishna Mandir, frying black-lentil bara on the same tawa for 60-70 years. Cash only, they cook a set quantity and stop when it goes, and the same family runs a second Honacha 20 m away by the Bhimsen Temple that no map pin separates — expect to ask

items.title: Nag Bahal courtyard
items.notes: Free, unticketed and open at any hour, immediately beside the Golden Temple about 320 m north-north-west of Durbar Square — not south, where some listings put it. A living neighbourhood: walk clockwise around the chaityas and ask before close-ups of residents

items.title: Kumbheshwar Technical School
items.notes: Fair-trade weaving and craft, best seen 10:00-15:00 while the looms are running. Their published week is Sunday-Thursday, but Nepal moved to a Saturday-Sunday government weekend in April 2026 and the listing may not have caught up — phone +977 1 5537484 ahead

items.title: kar.ma Coffee, Jhamsikhel
items.notes: Nepal's benchmark third-wave roaster, buying single-origin lots direct from mid-hill farming families. It is on Level 2 of the Gyan Mandala building and invisible from street level — look for the stairs; beans to take home and cards accepted

items.title: Golden-hour street photography in Patan
items.notes: Warm side light filters through the narrow streets and brick facades; sunset is about 17:15, so the good window is short and then it is gone

items.title: Dinner at Raithaane, Kupondole
items.notes: Modern Nepali as preservation rather than fusion, built on heritage grains bought direct from farmers. The kitchen closes about 20:30 so this is the sitting; reserve on +977 9801002971, and note it has moved from the Saugal courtyard address that maps still carry

items.title: Sam's Bar social night
items.notes: Cheap drinks, pool tables and a mix of travelers — Thamel's easiest casual night. Verify hours/cover before going.

items.title: Pre-dawn drive to Nagarkot
items.notes: Early departure to reach the ridge before first light. It is 2-8C up there at dawn and 18-20C by midday — layers, not a heavy coat

items.title: Himalayan sunrise at the Nagarkot view tower
items.notes: On the rim you are above the overnight inversion, so Everest, Langtang and Ganesh Himal stay sharp from first light to about 09:00 and wash out after 10:00 — the opposite of the valley floor. Sunrise is about 06:45; telephoto 70-200mm and a tripod

items.title: Mountain breakfast at Club Himalaya
items.notes: Relaxed breakfast with the range still in view; Bhaktapur is about 45 minutes back down the ridge

items.title: Bhaktapur Durbar Square
items.notes: Best-preserved medieval city in the valley — the 55-Window Palace and Nyatapola Temple. Buy the NPR 1,800 foreigner ticket here and show your passport at the gate: it extends to a week free, which covers the return visit on the 16th

items.title: Lunch at Aama ko Bara Pasal, Taumadhi
items.notes: A two-metre-wide shopfront beside Nyatapola that has made bara since the early 1970s — cash only, no English menu, tiny and unheated, and a fixed daily quantity that goes. There is no map node for the shop, so ask in Taumadhi rather than trusting a dot

items.title: Bhaktapur Pottery Square
items.notes: The full drying ground is out 11:00-14:00, and the enclosed square sits in cold flat shade until about 09:00 — which is why it belongs here and not at dawn. Stay on the perimeter, do not walk between the drying pots, and ask before close-ups of the potters

items.title: Juju Dhau (King Curd) tasting
items.notes: The famous Bhaktapur sweet yogurt served in a clay pot — a must-try

items.title: Bibaha Panchami at Ram Mandir, Battisputali
items.notes: Kathmandu's main Ram temple, and the re-enacted wedding of Ram and Sita falls today, Monday 14 December 2026 — the only major dated Hindu festival inside the trip. The date is confirmed but the scale of the Kathmandu observance is documented nowhere and it may be a modest neighbourhood puja, so treat it as a detour with upside: come off the highway at Gaushala on the return leg rather than making a separate trip. Modest dress, shoes off inside

items.title: Quiet dinner in Thamel
items.notes: Low-key evening after a 05:00 start — the next three days all run long

items.title: Breakfast at Chikusa Cafe, Jyatha
items.notes: Open since 1998 with no espresso machine at all, on purpose — everything is cloth-filter drip, moka pot or French press, so do not turn up wanting a flat white. Food is made to order and slow by design; cash is easiest, and it is about 10 minutes' walk from the hotel

items.title: Chandragiri Hills cable car
items.notes: Cable car up to the valley rim; hours are 08:00-17:00 on weekdays, shorter than some listings claim. Bring layers — the top is genuinely cold in December

items.title: Summit photography from the Chandragiri rim
items.notes: Above the overnight inversion again: the peaks hold sharp until about 09:00 and soften after 10:00, so shoot the ridge line first and the valley second. Telephoto for compressed ridges

items.title: Walk down the far side to Chitlang
items.notes: The trailhead at the top station is an unsigned path beside the men's bathroom between the yellow snack shops: down the stairs to a road, left at the police checkpoint, then ask further down for the steep trail into the woods. December has no mud and no leeches, which is why nobody walks this June to September

items.title: Lunch, the Newar village and the goat-cheese farm in Chitlang
items.notes: The pin marks a village strung along about a kilometre of valley, not a building — navigate to a named target such as Chitlang Organic Village Resort. The goat-cheese farm is a family homestay rather than a shop with fixed hours, so call ahead or you may arrive to a closed door

items.title: Drive back to Kathmandu via the Kulekhani road
items.notes: The return leg is about two hours. Agree the pickup point with the driver before leaving Thamel — the whole day lives or dies on him knowing where the trail comes out

items.title: Dinner at Tukche Thakali Kitchen, Gairidhara
items.notes: Family-run since 1997 and spiced closer to a real Thakali set than the milder chain versions; open to 21:00, a 10-minute taxi from Thamel. Dhedo and the hot black-lentil dal are the right order after a day on the ridge

items.title: Live music at House of Music
items.notes: Thamel's most consistent live-music calendar, and a short night after eight hours on foot. Verify hours/cover before going.

items.title: Changu Narayan Temple
items.notes: The oldest Hindu temple in the valley and a UNESCO site — 5th-century stone and woodcarving. Kept to about an hour: the weight of the day is Panauti, and the hilltop is cold and shaded this early

items.title: Kailashnath Mahadev Statue, Sanga
items.notes: Nepal's tallest Shiva statue, not the world's — the 112 m Vishwas Swaroopam at Nathdwara took that in 2022, though nearly every Nepali listing still says otherwise. Grounds open 07:30; the motorable road ends at the Hilltake gate at NPR 100, while the separate footpath gate to the left is nominally free

items.title: Drive to Panauti
items.notes: Araniko Highway to Banepa and then south, sealed the whole way. Carry cash for the day — there is no ATM out here worth relying on

items.title: Panauti
items.notes: Some of Nepal's oldest surviving pagoda temples, a street plan on UNESCO's tentative list, and almost no other foreigners in frame. The NPR 300 combined ticket covers the Indreshwar complex and the volunteer-run museum 40 m away in the same courtyard; the 20-minute stair climb to the hilltop viewpoint above town is worth adding

items.title: Lunch in Panauti
items.notes: Simple local food near the Indreshwar complex before the drive back west

items.title: Drive back to Bhaktapur
items.notes: Back via Banepa to reach Bhaktapur for the last hour of light

items.title: Golden hour in Bhaktapur Durbar Square
items.notes: Free re-entry on the week ticket bought on the 14th — show the same ticket and your passport at the gate. Sunset is about 17:15, so the warm light across the brick is short

items.title: Dinner at Restaurant TUSA
items.notes: Twelve covers and seven courses in a rebuilt Newari courtyard house, on a single strict seating window of 17:30-19:30. It books weeks ahead with a 50% advance, so reserve long before arrival on +977 9821055559 or at tusanepal.com, and confirm they are trading in December 2026

items.title: Fat Monk's Rooftop Bar
items.notes: Back in Thamel after the run east — a rooftop, so take a layer, and Thamel bars wind down ~23:00-midnight. Verify hours/cover before going.

items.title: Pre-dawn climb to Phulchowki
items.notes: The valley's highest rim peak, blanketed in rhododendron forest — layered ridge-lines and a Himalayan panorama. You are above the overnight inversion up here, so it holds sharp until about 09:00 and washes out after 10:00; it is 2-8C at the top before sunrise

items.title: Godavari Botanical Garden
items.notes: Peaceful gardens at the foot of Phulchowki — a flat stroll to walk off the descent

items.title: Lunch in Godavari
items.notes: Refuel before crossing the south valley to Khokana

items.title: Khokana and the mustard-oil mills
items.notes: A medieval street plan still intact, with a mustard-oil industry worked on a wooden beam press — ask specifically for the traditional press, because most mills here are motorised now. Mill floors are hot, dark and crowded with no guardrails; watch your feet and ask before photographing workers

items.title: Bungamati woodcarvers' village
items.notes: A 20-25 minute walk from Khokana over the Karya Binayak ridge, which is a valley viewpoint in its own right. The Rato Machhindranath idol is in residence here for the whole trip window — Yomari Punhi falls on 24 December, six days after departure. Be discreet with the camera near the army camp on the village edge

items.title: Chobhar Gorge & Jal Binayak
items.notes: The gorge where the Bagmati cuts the valley rim — vintage suspension bridge and a riverside temple, in soft side light after 15:00

items.title: Taudaha Lake birdwatching
items.notes: Late afternoon is the lake's best hour and December is peak for migratory birds; tea stalls along the shore

items.title: Dinner at Chez Caroline, Baber Mahal Revisited
items.notes: French bistro in the courtyard of a restored Rana palace and stable complex, sharing it with the Siddhartha Art Gallery. Reserve on 01-5363070 and ask for an indoor table — the courtyard is cold after sunset; allow 30-40 minutes to walk the arcades

items.title: Kathmandu send-off at Club Fahrenheit
items.notes: The last Nepal night — Thursday is Fahrenheit's/LOD's night. Verify hours/cover before going.

items.title: Rani Pokhari at first light
items.notes: Open 05:00-16:00 and free, so there is no sunset shot here — the water is dead still at dawn instead. Reopened to the public in March 2025; guidebooks saying it is shut all year are out of date, and the temple in the middle only opens on Bhai Tika, so shoot it across the water

items.title: Dharahara observation deck
items.notes: Book the timed slot ahead at dharahara.gov.np — daily entries are capped and slots sell out; arrive 30 minutes early. The deck is on the 20th floor (older write-ups say the 8th, which belonged to the tower that fell in 2015) and 08:00-09:30 is the mountain window

items.title: Kathmandu Durbar Square
items.notes: UNESCO royal square — Hanuman Dhoka, the temple plinths and the living goddess at Kumari Ghar. The valley haze is thinnest now and thickens again through the afternoon

items.title: Itum Bahal courtyard
items.notes: An unmarked low doorway straight off the Thamel-to-Durbar-Square walk, opening into a lived-in monastery courtyard. Enclosed on four sides, so it only works once the sun clears the walls; ask before photographing residents, keep out of doorways and walk clockwise around the chaityas

items.title: Asan Bazaar
items.notes: Oldest market in the city — spices, fabrics and hidden temples packed into six converging lanes; ask permission for portraits

items.title: Lunch in Thamel
items.notes: Easy bite back at the hotel end between the old city and the afternoon

items.title: Museum of Nepali Art
items.notes: Paubha and thangka shown as art rather than as souvenirs, three minutes' walk from Thamel and open daily 10:00-18:00. Entrance from the EAST GATE only, not the Kathmandu Guest House lobby; the ticket is valid all day for re-entry and cash is safest

items.title: Souvenir shopping in Thamel & Asan
items.notes: Pashmina, singing bowls, Nepali tea, prayer flags and handmade paper — last gifts before Japan

items.title: Check out and collect the bags
items.notes: Settle up and load the luggage into the vehicle now, so the evening runs straight on to the airport with nothing to come back for

items.title: Pashupatinath evening aarti
items.notes: The riverside aarti on the Bagmati ghats; non-Hindus cannot enter the main shrine, and the cremation ghats need photographing with restraint. Bags are already in the vehicle and the temple is about 3 km from the airport, so this is on the way out, not a detour

items.title: Transfer to Tribhuvan (KTM)
items.notes: Straight from Pashupatinath to the international terminal for the late-night departure

items.title: Depart Kathmandu (KTM) → Guangzhou (CAN) — Overnight connection
items.notes: KTM Terminal I → CAN Terminal 2 · Overnight connection · arrives 5:55am Dec 19 · Economy. Overnight flight — sleep if you can

items.title: Layover at Guangzhou (CAN) Terminal 2
items.notes: Early-morning connection at Baiyun Intl before the flight to Tokyo

items.title: Fly Guangzhou (CAN) → Tokyo Haneda (HND) — Connecting flight to Tokyo
items.notes: CAN T2 → HND Terminal 3 · Connecting flight to Tokyo · arrives 1:35pm · Economy. Fill out Visit Japan Web before landing

items.title: Immigration, baggage & transfer to Haneda domestic terminal (T1)
items.notes: Clear immigration and collect baggage after the international arrival, then transfer across Haneda to the domestic terminal (T1) to check in for the Osaka flight

items.title: Fly Tokyo Haneda (HND) → Osaka Itami (ITM) — Domestic hop to Osaka
items.notes: HND Terminal 1 → ITM · Domestic hop to Osaka · arrives 5:35pm · Economy (Q). Real booked domestic flight — render the times exactly as booked

items.title: Check in to the Shinsaibashi hotel
items.notes: Real booked hotel in Shinsaibashi. Official check-in is 15:00 and the flight lands at 17:35, so the room is already waiting — the airport limousine bus from Itami to the Namba terminal is about 25 minutes and the hotel is a short walk on from there

items.title: Dotonbori and the Glico Running Man
items.notes: Sunset was 16:50, so the canal is already fully dark and nothing outdoor has been lost to the late landing. Shoot the sign from Ebisu Bridge, directly opposite it — that is the frame everyone comes for, and a slow shutter turns the canal into a mirror of the neon. Public street, always on, five minutes from the hotel

items.title: Dinner and drinks in Hozenji Yokocho
items.notes: A lantern-lit stone alley behind Hozenji Temple, two minutes off the Dotonbori crowd, with about sixty izakaya and kushikatsu counters along it. Most of them shut between 22:00 and 23:00, so this is the early half of the night and not the late one. Small counters — walking the lane and taking the first place with three free seats beats holding out for one particular door

items.title: Giraffe
items.notes: Steps from the Glico sign, unpretentious and party-first with a mixed tourist and local floor — the right first-night room because nobody has to dress for it or commit to a long night after thirty hours in transit. Top 40 and hip-hop. Last trains in Osaka run to roughly 00:00 and first trains from about 05:00, but the hotel is a walk from here so neither matters tonight. Verify the door charge before going in

items.title: Osaka Castle keep and moat
items.notes: Open 09:00-17:00 with last entry at 16:30, and this is the window: the keep closes Dec 28 to Jan 1 every year and reopens Jan 2 at 09:00, by which time the party is in Tokyo. Winter strips the plum grove bare, which keeps the sightlines across the moat open — shoot the keep from the far bank for the reflection

items.title: Lunch on the Dotonbori canal
items.notes: Fifteen minutes back from Tanimachi 4-chome. Takoyaki, okonomiyaki and negiyaki from the canal-front stands, eaten standing up. Osaka has no reservation culture at this end of the market and no queue worth planning around at lunch — the evening is when it backs up

items.title: Shinsaibashi-suji arcade and Amerikamura
items.notes: The long covered arcade runs north from Dotonbori and is at its busiest on a Sunday, with no seasonal closure to work around. Amerikamura, one block west, is the streetwear quarter — vintage, sneakers and record shops around Triangle Park. Note that Soemoncho, the strip immediately east of the canal, is adult-nightlife-adjacent with unclear pricing and persistent touts: walk through it, do not stop for a drink

items.title: Umeda Sky Building — Floating Garden Observatory
items.notes: Two stops north on the Midosuji line and a nine-minute walk. An open-air rooftop deck at 173 m with a waist-high barrier and nothing overhead, which is why the escalator across the void between the two towers is the shot as much as the view is. Sunset is 16:50 and full dark about 17:20, so arriving now buys the whole transition. Handheld only — tripods are not allowed up there

items.title: Osaka Hikari-Renaissance, Nakanoshima
items.notes: A fifteen-minute walk south from Umeda onto the Nakanoshima sandbar. Projection mapping on the 1918 Central Public Hall plus a tunnel of light along the riverside path — a December-only event that on the 2025-26 pattern ran Dec 14-31, so it overlaps the whole Osaka leg. Free, and the tripod is welcome here even though it was not on the roof. Confirm the 2026 dates when they post in November

items.title: Dotonbori food crawl
items.notes: Back south on the Midosuji line from Yodoyabashi, ten minutes. The proper crawl this time rather than the lunchtime version — kushikatsu, ikayaki, a crab from one of the signed shopfronts, and the canal at full brightness on the way through

items.title: Nihonshu Unagidani
items.notes: A standing sake bar near Shinsaibashi Station with more than a hundred bottles in glass-fronted fridges you pick from yourself. Cheap, quick and a genuine local room rather than a club warm-up bar — one round here before the floor fills up next door

items.title: Club Bambi
items.notes: The first proper club night, and a Sunday: the big Shinsaibashi rooms programme Friday and Saturday, so a young cheap hip-hop-inclusive floor is the honest pick tonight rather than a flagship with nobody in it. Check tonight's actual event before walking there and agree the cover and any drink minimum at the door. Kinryu Ramen on Dotonbori runs 24 hours and is the walk home

items.title: Shinsaibashi → Universal City
items.notes: Midosuji line to Umeda, walk through to JR Osaka, Loop line to Nishikujo, then the Yumesaki line two stops to Universal City. About 40 minutes with the transfers, and the gate queue is what the extra five minutes are for

items.title: Universal Studios Japan — Super Nintendo World
items.notes: The single most booking-sensitive day of the trip. Three things have to be bought and they are not the same purchase: a dated Studio Pass, an Express Pass, and a Super Nintendo World Area Timed Entry ticket unless the Express Pass already bundles one. Express Passes release roughly 60 days out, one new date per day at 00:00, which puts Dec 21 at around 21 Oct 2026 and the good passes go first. Same-day timed entry now runs through the park app, so at least one phone needs data and the app installed before the gate, not in the queue. The published operating calendar sets the day's hours about two months out — do not assume 09:00-21:00

items.title: Lunch inside the park
items.notes: Eat at the back of the lunch rush rather than the front of it — the Nintendo World restaurants are the bottleneck and the rest of the park empties out between 12:00 and 13:00

items.title: Afternoon rides and the evening parade
items.notes: Dec 21 is a Monday and falls before the Japanese school winter holidays, which start around Dec 25 — this is the good half of December and the reason the park day sits here and not later in the trip. Check the current anime and game collaborations when the date gets close; they rotate and they are the thing this group would actually queue for

items.title: Late dinner at Kinryu Ramen, Dotonbori
items.notes: Back on the canal about 19:30 after the park. Open 24 hours, order from the machine, eat standing or on the tatami platform out front, help yourself to the kimchi and chives on the counter. The right end to a fourteen-hour day on foot

items.title: Karaoke box in Namba
items.notes: A deliberately lower-output night between two big ones. Big Echo and Karaoke Kan both have Namba and Shinsaibashi branches, they take three people into a private room without a wait on a Monday, and the hourly rate is a fraction of a club door. Drinks are ordered to the room, so nobody is standing at a bar

items.title: Shinsaibashi → Osakako
items.notes: Midosuji line one stop to Hommachi, then the Chuo line west to Osakako. The aquarium is a five-minute walk from the exit

items.title: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
items.notes: Built as a single spiral descent around a 9 m-deep central Pacific tank holding whale sharks, so the same tank is seen from eight different depths on the way down. Broadly 10:00-20:00 with seasonal variation and last entry an hour before closing — Kaiyukan publishes a per-date calendar, so check the actual day rather than the general hours. Buy a timed e-ticket: it is cheaper than the gate and the gate queue on a holiday afternoon is long. Indoors, which is the point on a cold December day

items.title: Lunch on the Tempozan quay
items.notes: Eat here rather than carrying the appetite back into town — the quay has the food floors, the Ferris wheel and the harbour ferry terminal all on the same block, and backtracking to Namba for lunch costs an hour of the shopping afternoon

items.title: Tempozan → Nipponbashi
items.notes: Chuo line back east to Sakaisuji-Hommachi, then the Sakaisuji line south to Nipponbashi. About 25 minutes

items.title: Den Den Town figure and manga run
items.notes: Osaka's answer to Akihabara, strung along Sakaisuji between Nipponbashi and Ebisucho. Shops run roughly 11:00-20:00 with no December closure, and the useful pattern is that the big chains sit on the main street while the second-hand and garage-kit dealers are one block back. One Piece, Naruto and Dragon Ball are everywhere; the things worth the trip are the used-figure floors and the gachapon walls, which turn over faster here than in Tokyo

items.title: Dinner on Dotonbori
items.notes: A ten-minute walk north from Den Den Town puts the group back on the canal without a train. Okonomiyaki tonight if the crawl on the 20th did takoyaki — the two are not interchangeable and Osaka will tell you so

items.title: Amerikamura bars
items.notes: Amemura is the youth-culture quarter — streetwear by day, hip-hop and rap-leaning bars at night, cheaper and less touristed than the Shinsaibashi club row a block east. A Tuesday is exactly the night for it: small rooms with a crowd rather than a big room without one

items.title: Pure Osaka
items.notes: A Dotonbori-area room, deliberately rotated off Sunday's Shinsaibashi floor so the two club nights are not the same night twice. Tuesday is quiet everywhere in Osaka, so check tonight's event before committing — and if the floor is dead, Amerikamura is a four-minute walk back

items.title: Shinsaibashi → Kintetsu-Nara
items.notes: One stop or an eight-minute walk to Osaka-Namba, then a Kintetsu Rapid Express straight through to Kintetsu-Nara in 35-38 minutes, six an hour. The Rapid Express needs no reservation — only the Limited Express does, and it saves about five minutes for the price of a seat ticket. Door to door about 1h15, the shortest real day trip on the whole trip

items.title: Nakatanidou
items.notes: Four hundred metres from the station on Sanjo-dori, so it costs ten minutes on the walk in rather than a detour. Warm yomogi mochi sold one piece at a time over the counter at about 150-200 yen. The two-man high-speed mallet demonstration outside is what the crowds film, but it runs on no published timetable — treat it as luck, not as an item to wait for

items.title: Nara Park and the walk up to Nandaimon
items.notes: The deer come right up the approach path and will bow for a shika-senbei cracker, which is the whole reason to shoot with an 85mm here rather than a wide. They also head-butt for the crackers, so hand them over rather than negotiating. The park itself is free

items.title: Todai-ji Daibutsuden
items.notes: The largest wooden temple hall in the world, holding a 15 m bronze Buddha cast in 752. Open 08:00-17:00 from November to March with no closing days, 800 yen for the hall while the park around it stays free. The pillar at the back with a hole cut through its base is sized to the Buddha's nostril and there is usually a queue of children going through it

items.title: Lunch on the Higashimuki arcade
items.notes: The covered arcade between Kintetsu-Nara Station and the park, which is where Nara actually eats — kakinoha-zushi wrapped in persimmon leaf, udon, and the narezushi counters. Nothing here needs booking and nothing here closes in December

items.title: Nara Park at low light
items.notes: Sunset is 16:51 and the reality is that the park has to be finished by 16:00 — the light goes flat under the trees well before it goes off the sky. Side light through the cedar avenue between Nandaimon and the Kasuga approach is the best hour of the day here

items.title: Kintetsu-Nara → Shinsaibashi
items.notes: Straight back the way it came. Himeji Castle was the alternative shape for today — 1h50 door to door and genuinely better architecture, but last admission is 16:00 with no re-entry, so it would have meant leaving before midday and losing the evening. It is also shut Dec 29-30, its only two closing days of the year, which kills any idea of going back for it later

items.title: Kushikatsu under Tsutenkaku, Shinsekai
items.notes: Ten minutes down the Midosuji line to Ebisucho. Shinsekai is the 1912 retro quarter under the Tsutenkaku tower and kushikatsu is its dish — deep-fried skewers with a communal sauce tub on every table, and the one rule that matters is no double-dipping. Cabbage on the table is free and is what you use to scoop more sauce

items.title: Club Joule
items.notes: The last Osaka night, so the biggest room on the strip: three floors in Shinsaibashi with an 800-capacity main floor, a mezzanine and a rooftop terrace, EDM through hip-hop. It is a Wednesday, so check the actual listing before committing the night to it — GHOST Ultra Lounge and Gala Resort are the two fallbacks within the same few blocks. Pace it: checkout is 11:00 tomorrow and the bags have to be packed

items.title: Check out of the Shinsaibashi hotel
items.notes: Real booked checkout is 11:00 — bags down and settled before then. Nothing about today needs an earlier start, because the Kyoto room is not available until 14:00 either way

items.title: Osaka → Kyoto by Hankyu
items.notes: Midosuji line to Osaka-Umeda, then a Hankyu Kyoto Line Limited Express straight to Kyoto-Kawaramachi in about 45 minutes for around 410 yen. This is the better train than the JR Special Rapid today: it is slower to Kyoto Station but it terminates directly under the Shijo-Kawaramachi crossing, which is where the hotel is, so it saves a second transfer with three suitcases

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.notes: Leave the bags at the hotel desk on the way past — check-in is not until 14:00. The market is a covered arcade five blocks long, 350 m from the crossing, typically 10:00-18:00 store by store. A good number of stalls close on Wednesdays and Dec 24 is a Thursday, so that does not bite today. Eat standing at the stall: tamagoyaki on a stick, soy-milk doughnuts, grilled scallops, hamo tempura

items.title: Check in to the Shijo-Kawaramachi hotel
items.notes: Real booked check-in is 14:00, at the Shijo-Kawaramachi crossing. Everything on the Kyoto leg except Arashiyama and Fushimi is inside a 25-minute radius of this door, which is why the evenings can run late here without a taxi plan

items.title: Nijo Castle and the Ninomaru Palace
items.notes: Hankyu one stop to Karasuma, Karasuma line to Karasuma-Oike, Tozai line to Nijojo-mae — about 25 minutes. Go straight to the palace and do the moat afterwards: the castle takes last entry at 16:00 but the Ninomaru Palace reception shuts at 16:10 and that is the hard cut. This is the last chance for it — the Ninomaru and Honmaru interiors both close Dec 26-28, and Ninomaru also closes every Tuesday in December. 800 yen for the grounds, 1,300 with Ninomaru; the Honmaru needs a separate advance reservation and is shut Dec 26-28 regardless. The nightingale floors are the reason to pay the extra 500

items.title: Kyoto Station building and the Daikaidan light show
items.notes: Twenty minutes from Nijojo-mae. The Daikaidan is a 171-step staircase cut up the east side of the station atrium with LEDs set into every riser; the light show runs on it through the evening and costs nothing. The observation deck on the tower opposite runs 10:00-21:00 with last entry 20:30 if the group wants the paid version, and the 10th-floor ramen street runs roughly 11:00-22:00. All of it survives the New Year shutdown, which almost nothing else in Kyoto does

items.title: Christmas Eve dinner at Menami
items.notes: An obanzai counter on Kiyamachi, one street back from Pontocho: the day's dishes are set out in bowls along the counter and you point. Open 15:00-22:00 with last order 21:30, closed Wednesdays, so Dec 24 is fine. Two things about booking it — Christmas Eve is the single biggest restaurant night of the Japanese year and a walk-in trio will be turned away, and Menami takes bookings by phone only, in the afternoon, in Japanese. Somebody has to make that call, and it has to happen in early December

items.title: Pontocho Alley
items.notes: Two minutes from the restaurant. A single lane barely two metres wide between the Kamo River and Kiyamachi, wooden fronts and lanterns the whole length. Shoot it from the Sanjo end looking south with a fast prime — it is narrow enough that a wide lens just gets you walls. Some doors here carry a seating charge or take regulars only, so a posted menu or an English sign is the signal that a place will seat three

items.title: Rocking Bar ING
items.notes: A dive rock bar on Kiyamachi-dori run by the same owner for more than twenty years, walls buried in Rolling Stones memorabilia — the counterpoint to a night that has otherwise been all lanterns and machiya. Kyoto's subway stops around 23:30-23:50 and the city buses are largely finished by 22:30, but the hotel is a seven-minute walk from this door, which is the entire reason the Kyoto nights are based here

items.title: Kawaramachi → Fushimi Inari
items.notes: Five minutes on foot east over Shijo bridge to Keihan Gion-Shijo, then a local or semi-express south to Fushimi-Inari — the limited expresses do not stop there. First Keihan services run from about 05:20, so this works

items.title: Dawn at Fushimi Inari
items.notes: Civil dawn is 06:35 and sunrise is 07:03, so 06:30 is right for arriving and wrong for shooting. The lower torii route has footpath lighting and lanterns — enough to walk by, not enough to shoot by — so bring a torch and expect the first twenty minutes to be a walk. Usable frames start around 06:50 and the empty-tunnel window then runs to about 08:00. The mountain trail above Yotsutsuji is genuinely dark, with a standing local warning about wild boar and advice not to go up alone, so stay on the lit lower loop until it is light. Grounds are free and open around the clock; the shrine office and amulet counters only open around 07:00

items.title: Breakfast at Inoda Coffee Honten
items.notes: Back north to Gion-Shijo and twelve minutes west on foot. Inoda opens at 07:00, which is why it cannot be breakfast on the way out to the shrine and works perfectly on the way back. Open every day of the year. Order the Arabian Pearl — it comes with milk and sugar already in it by house default, which catches people out — and sit in the old round-counter room rather than the annexe

items.title: Kyoto International Manga Museum
items.notes: A ten-minute walk north to Karasuma-Oike. A 1920s elementary school converted into a manga library, corridors walled floor to ceiling with about 300,000 volumes that visitors are free to pull down and read on the stairs or the lawn. 10:00-17:00, last admission 16:30, 1,200 yen. Today is the last day it can be seen on this trip: the museum's own calendar closes it from 2026/12/26 to 2027/1/6. Most of the collection is Japanese-only, with a smaller shelf of translated and foreign work

items.title: Karasuma-Oike → Kiyomizu-michi
items.notes: Subway back to Shijo, then the 100 or 206 bus east to Kiyomizu-michi and a ten-minute walk up the hill. The buses run every few minutes and are the slow part; a taxi is about fifteen minutes and worth it for three people if one is behind schedule

items.title: Kiyomizu-dera
items.notes: Founded in 780 above the Otowa waterfall, and the wooden stage projects out over the valley on a lattice of pillars driven together without a single nail. 500 yen, opens at 06:00 daily and closes about 18:00 in winter, with no closing days all year — it is open two hours before almost anything else in Kyoto, which makes it the better dawn target than Fushimi if the group ever wants to swap. The special night viewings are spring and autumn only, so there is nothing to book in December

items.title: Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka
items.notes: Two stone-stepped lanes of preserved machiya running downhill from Kiyomizu towards Kodai-ji, tea shops and sweet stalls the whole way — this is where the afternoon eating happens, on the hoof. Shops run roughly 09:00-18:00 and start pulling shutters once it goes dark, which is 17:20. The five-storey Yasaka Pagoda stands about 200 m below the foot of Ninenzaka and closes most of the frames shot along here. The steps are worn and slick in the wet; the name Sannenzaka carries a local superstition about falling on them

items.title: Saryo Tsujiri, Gion Honten
items.notes: Ten minutes down from the foot of Ninenzaka and directly on the Gion walk. Uji matcha parfaits and warabi mochi from a house that has been in tea since 1860. No reservations and there is a queue; posted hours have moved more than once in recent years, so check the door rather than a listing. Tearoom last order is around 20:00 on a weekday

items.title: Hanamikoji-dori after dark
items.notes: Full dark is 17:20 and the paper lanterns are lit by then, which is the only reason this is an evening item rather than an afternoon one. Kyoto fines photography on the private side alleys off this street at 10,000 yen, and photographing geiko or maiko without their consent is not permitted at all — the shooting happens from the public street, pointed at architecture. The ochaya along here are introduction-only and cannot be booked, so this is a walk, not a booking

items.title: Christmas dinner at Tempura Yoshikawa
items.notes: Twenty minutes west across Shijo bridge, or ten by taxi. An eight-seat counter in a ryokan garden where the chef fries each piece in front of you and puts it straight on your paper. Dinner runs 17:30-19:30 and is bookable, which the lunch counter is not — the 12:00-13:30 lunch sitting takes no reservations at all and would have collided head-on with Kiyomizu, which is why it is dinner or nothing. Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays; Friday Dec 25 is open. This is a real bill, so decide before booking rather than at the counter

items.title: Rokudenashi
items.notes: A first-floor-up jazz bar on Kiyamachi run by a working drummer for about forty years — a room where the records are the point and the conversation is quiet. Kyoto has no hip-hop floor worth the trip and pretending otherwise wastes a night; this is what the city is actually good at. Ten minutes on foot from the hotel

items.title: Kawaramachi → Arashiyama
items.notes: Hankyu from Kyoto-Kawaramachi to Katsura, change for the Arashiyama branch, then a ten-minute walk over the river. First services run from about 05:40, so a 07:00 arrival at the grove is realistic

items.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
items.notes: Sunrise is 07:04, so the first fifteen minutes are pre-dawn and the path is unlit — it is a public right of way with no gate and no fee, which is exactly why arriving before 08:00 is the only reliable way to have it to yourselves. The crowd argument holds until about 08:30. Point the camera straight up for the canopy; at eye level it is a corridor of people by nine. The December Hanatouro illumination that older guides sell here has not run in its original form since 2021 and even then finished around Dec 19 — do not plan on it

items.title: Tenryu-ji and the Cloud Dragon
items.notes: The grove path runs straight out of the back of this temple. Open 08:30-17:00, last admission 16:50, year round; 500 yen for the Sogenchi pond garden, 800 with the buildings. The Cloud Dragon painted on the Hatto ceiling is a separate 500-yen ticket and is only open to the public at weekends and on holidays — Dec 26 is a Saturday, which is the whole reason Arashiyama is today and not a weekday. The garden keeps Muso Soseki's fourteenth-century layout and borrows the Arashiyama hills as its back wall

items.title: Togetsukyo Bridge
items.notes: A 155 m timber-clad bridge across the Katsura at the mouth of the Hozu gorge, and the crossing point to the monkey park, so it is a waypoint as much as a photograph. In late December the hills behind it are bare and brown rather than green and the sun drops behind the ridge by about 16:00 — the light on the water is a morning thing here

items.title: Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama
items.notes: Immediately across the bridge, then a twenty-minute climb up a steep path — the macaques are at the top, not the gate. Winter hours are 09:00-16:00, it closes in heavy rain or snow, the gate is cash only and there are no advance tickets. Feeding is only allowed inside the hut at the summit and only with the 100-yen bags sold there. The view back over Kyoto from the feeding ground is the second reason to climb it

items.title: Yudofu lunch at Yudofu Sagano
items.notes: Simmering tofu hot-pot in tatami rooms round a garden, which is the Arashiyama winter dish and comfortably seats three. Open 11:00-17:30 with last order 16:30, but it keeps irregular holidays — meaning it can be shut on the day with no notice, so have the Togetsukyo-end soba shops as the fallback. The multi-course version needs two days of notice; the standard set is walk-in

items.title: Arashiyama → Kinkaku-ji
items.notes: About 40 minutes across the north-west of the city — the Randen tram to Kitano-Hakubaicho then the 205 bus, or a straight taxi. There is no fast rail connection between these two, which is why pairing them in one day works but leaves no slack

items.title: Kinkaku-ji
items.notes: Two floors sheathed in gold leaf, mirrored in the Kyoko-chi pond. 09:00-17:00 daily, open every day of the year including through Dec 29 to Jan 3, 500 yen. The route through the grounds is one-way and takes about 40 minutes, so there is no going back for a second look at the pond — get the frame on the first pass. Afternoon light puts the sun behind the pavilion; the reflection is better than the facade at this hour

items.title: Kinkaku-ji → Kawaramachi
items.notes: The 205 bus from Kinkakuji-michi runs all the way down to Shijo-Kawaramachi in about 40 minutes. It is slow and it is full at this hour, and it is still the simplest way back

items.title: Nishiki Market at its loudest
items.notes: Worth a second pass rather than a first: a Saturday in the last week of December is the market at its most alive all year, because this is the week Kyoto shops for osechi and the vendors are calling prices down the arcade. It shuts at 18:00. Its actual peak is Dec 28-31, by which time the party is in Tokyo, and then most stalls close Jan 1-4

items.title: Dinner at Giro Giro Hitoshina
items.notes: A ten-minute walk south along the canal. A kaiseki counter run by young cooks with the pretension taken out of it — a set course, plated in front of you, at a fraction of what the form usually costs. Open 17:30-23:00, closed the last Monday of the month, which in December 2026 is the 28th and so is not a factor. Reservations are effectively required and a Saturday wants one to four weeks of notice, so this is one to book from Nepal

items.title: Sent James Club
items.notes: A riverside jazz bar in Pontocho running since 1983, with a terrace over the Kamo. The mellow half of the last Kyoto night, and it sits directly between dinner and the room below

items.title: Urbanguild
items.notes: A small performance space on Kiyamachi that programmes anything from jazz to experimental electronics, one night to the next — the closest Kyoto gets to a room this group would pick for itself. Check the calendar before going, because the booking genuinely changes the night. Last subway is 23:30-23:50 and the buses stopped an hour before that, but the hotel is walkable from here

items.title: Breakfast at Honke Daiichi Asahi
items.notes: Ten minutes by taxi down to Takabashi, by Kyoto Station. Open 06:00-01:00 and closed Thursdays — Dec 27 is a Sunday, so it is open, and it is the one genuinely early proper meal on the Kyoto leg. Kyoto-style shoyu ramen with a queue outside from before opening most days; going now rather than at the traditional 06:00 costs nothing but the queue

items.title: Check out of the Shijo-Kawaramachi hotel
items.notes: Real booked checkout is 11:00. Bags come with the group rather than into storage — the train is the next thing that happens

items.title: Kawaramachi → Kyoto Station
items.notes: The 4, 5 or 205 bus straight down Kawaramachi-dori, or the Karasuma subway from Shijo. Be early rather than exact: the oversized-baggage seats are at the end of the car, three suitcases take a moment to stow, and the year-end platform crush is not the place to be improvising

items.title: Kyoto → Tokyo by Shinkansen
items.notes: The one hard transport constraint of the trip. Every Nozomi runs all-reserved from 25 Dec 2026 to 5 Jan 2027, and Dec 27 sits inside that window — a non-reserved ticket does not buy a seat on a Nozomi, it buys standing room in the vestibule. Reserved seats opened one month ahead at 10:00 JST, so 27 Nov 2026, and three seats together on the Sunday of the year-end migration will not survive a casual approach. Three adults with checked-size suitcases also need the oversized-baggage seats at the end of the car: free, but they must be reserved with the ticket and there are only a handful per car. Hikari and Kodama keep their non-reserved cars and take about forty minutes longer. Right-side seats for the Fuji glimpse past Shizuoka

items.title: Tokyo Station → Shinjuku, and check in to the Kabukicho hotel
items.notes: Real booked check-in is 15:00. The Chuo Rapid runs Tokyo Station to Shinjuku in 14 minutes and the hotel is a short walk on from the east side. Thirteen nights in one room from here, which is the whole logic of the Tokyo leg: Kabukicho puts Golden Gai, Omoide Yokocho and the Shinjuku clubs inside a ten-minute walk, and the Yamanote inside five

items.title: Projection mapping on the Metropolitan Government Building
items.notes: A twenty-minute walk west of the hotel and free, with no ticket and no queue. Screenings run nightly through December and January at 17:30, 18:00, 18:30, 19:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:30 and 21:30, about fifteen minutes each, on a rotating programme that has included Godzilla, Gundam and Pokemon pieces. The observation decks in the same building are a separate thing and are shut Dec 29-31 and Jan 2-3 — Jan 1 is the only day in that stretch they open, so the deck is booked for then

items.title: Omoide Yokocho
items.notes: About sixty yakitori and offal counters wedged under the rail viaduct on the west side of Shinjuku Station. Grill smoke and lanterns from around 17:00, most stalls to midnight or 01:00, and mostly cash. Counters seat six to eight, so a walk-in trio on a Sunday evening will be split up or waiting — plan on two stalls rather than one, and treat the second as the plan rather than a defeat

items.title: Shinjuku Golden Gai
items.notes: Six narrow alleys of more than two hundred bars, each seating five to ten people, each with its own theme. Most open from 19:00. Two things to read off the door before going in: the seat charge, which runs 500-1,500 yen per person on top of the drinks, and whether the bar takes a group of three at all — a good number will not. An English-welcome sign is the reliable signal

items.title: T2 Shinjuku
items.notes: A big Kabukicho room that runs all week, which is the point on a Sunday when the Fri-Sat rooms are dark and Shibuya Yokocho closes at 23:00 instead of 05:00. Open-format. First night of thirteen — keep it short, the shape of the leg matters more than tonight does

items.title: Shinjuku → Asakusa
items.notes: Toei Shinjuku line east to Bakuro-yokoyama, then the Asakusa line; about 35 minutes. A full-day Hakone loop was the alternative shape for today and is genuinely good — Open-Air Museum, the Owakudani ropeway and the lake torii at Hakone Shrine — but it needs a 07:30 start, a Romancecar seat booked a month out, and the ropeway runs only 09:00-16:15 in December and January against 16:45 the rest of the year, so the loop barely closes. Today's east-Tokyo run is date-locked in a way Hakone is not, which is why it wins: Nakamise is still a shopping street rather than the one-way queue corridor it becomes from the evening of Dec 31 to Jan 3, and Ameyoko is in the loudest week of its year

items.title: Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori
items.notes: Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 645. In through the Kaminarimon under the four-metre lantern, up the Nakamise stalls to the main hall and the five-storey pagoda. Grounds are free and the main hall runs 06:00-17:00. Being here today rather than in the New Year window is deliberate — from the evening of Dec 31 to Jan 3 the approach is marshalled one-way for hatsumode and stops being a street you can browse

items.title: Suzukien Asakusa Honten
items.notes: Ten minutes north of the temple. Seven graded strengths of matcha gelato, with No. 7 sold as the strongest in the world — it is bitter enough that most people pair it with a weaker scoop rather than eating it alone. Open 10:00-17:00, closed the third Wednesday of the month, so today is fine. It shuts before dark, which is why it comes before the Skytree slot and not after

items.title: Ameya-Yokocho
items.notes: Five minutes on the Ginza line to Ueno. Four hundred-odd stalls under and beside the Yamanote viaduct, most of them 10:00-19:00. The last week of December is the loudest week of its year: this is when Tokyo buys crab, roe and osechi ingredients, and the vendors shout prices down as the day goes on. Lunch is the standing counters in here — kebabs, oden, seafood bowls — not a sit-down anywhere else

items.title: Tokyo Skytree
items.notes: Ginza line to Asakusa and one stop on the Tobu Skytree line, about 20 minutes. Open 10:00-21:00 with last entry 20:00. Sunset is 16:35, so a slot starting around 15:30 buys daylight, sunset and the city lit up from a single ticket — that is the whole reason for the time. Buy the timed ticket online, it is cheaper than the counter and skips the ground-floor queue. Tokyo National Museum is shut today for two independent reasons (closed Dec 26-31, and Mondays), which is why Ueno was a market stop rather than a museum one

items.title: JUMP SHOP Tokyo Solamachi
items.notes: The official Shonen Jump store, in the Solamachi mall at the foot of the tower, running on the mall's 10:00-21:00. One Piece, Naruto, Dragon Ball, Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer goods, a good share of it shop-exclusive and not in the Akihabara chains. Buy here rather than planning to find it later

items.title: Motsuyaki Daitoryo
items.notes: Back to Ueno, twenty minutes. Charcoal-grilled offal skewers and cheap highballs at plastic crates under the Ameyoko tracks, spilling into the street when the room is full — one of the last places in central Tokyo that still trades like this. Roughly 10:00 to midnight daily, though the published hours are secondary-source only, so confirm at the door. Cash. Ponta Honke, the tonkatsu house four minutes away, is shut on Mondays and is booked for tomorrow instead

items.title: DUG Jazz Cafe and Bar
items.notes: A sixty-year-old jazz kissa by the Shinjuku east exit, and the room Murakami put in Norwegian Wood. A Monday is the worst night of the week for the Kabukicho mega-clubs — they programme Friday and Saturday and a Monday floor is empty — so tonight is a bar with a reason to exist rather than a club without one. Twenty-five minutes back from Ueno on the Yamanote

items.title: Shinjuku → Tsukiji
items.notes: Marunouchi line to Ginza, then one stop on the Hibiya line. Draw cash today while it is easy: banks, post offices and most ATMs shut from roughly Dec 31 to Jan 3, and only the convenience-store machines keep working through it

items.title: Tsukiji Outer Market
items.notes: Trade starts around 06:00 and general shopping runs roughly 09:00-14:00, with stalls shutting through the early afternoon. Come knowing what today is: Dec 28-30 is the busiest stretch of its year and the market itself asks casual visitors to consider other days, so this is a crush, not a stroll. The last trading day is Dec 30, then it is closed Dec 31 to Jan 4 and reopens Jan 5. Tamagoyaki on a stick, uni, grilled scallop, a knife shop if anyone wants one. Toyosu, the wholesale market that replaced the inner one, is not on this plan: a 05:00 start does not survive a night out, and its January 2027 calendar was not published in time to promise a Wednesday

items.title: Sushi Zanmai Honten
items.notes: Open 24 hours and listed as open every day of the year, no reservations, at the entrance to the outer market. In a district full of two-seat counters and forty-minute queues, this is the one that seats three adults together at nine in the morning without an argument. Sit at the counter and order by piece rather than taking a set

items.title: Tsukiji → Ueno
items.notes: Hibiya line straight through, about fifteen minutes plus the walk. Aim to be at the restaurant door by 11:30

items.title: Ponta Honke
items.notes: A tonkatsu house that has been in Ueno since 1905 and effectively invented the dish — the katsu here is cut thick, fried pale and served without the sauce most places drown it in. Lunch runs 11:00-14:00 with last order 13:45 and it is closed Mondays, which is why it could not be yesterday. No reservations for a small group, so queue for the first sitting rather than turning up at one

items.title: Yanaka Ginza and the Yuyake Dandan steps
items.notes: Four minutes on the Yamanote to Nippori. A short shopping street of about seventy small shops in one of the few parts of central Tokyo that neither the 1945 firebombing nor the bubble flattened. The Yuyake Dandan steps at the top are the frame — the name means sunset steps and they face west down the street. Shops run roughly 10:00-18:00 and many close by dusk, and sunset is 16:35, so the honest window for the light is mid-afternoon rather than actual sunset. Menchi katsu and grilled rice balls from the street

items.title: Super Potato Akihabara
items.notes: Eight minutes down the Yamanote from Nippori. The retro game shop, roughly 11:00-20:00 — Famicom and Super Famicom carts by the wall, boxed hardware upstairs, and a floor of playable arcade cabinets at the top that most people miss because the stairs look like storage

items.title: Mandarake Complex Akihabara
items.notes: Eight floors, one specialism per floor, 12:00-20:00 daily and open year-round — which matters because it is one of the few Akihabara names that does not take a New Year break. Vintage figures, cels, doujinshi, Showa-era Jump. The buy-back counter closes at 19:30 if anyone wants to sell rather than buy

items.title: Akihabara Radio Kaikan
items.notes: The tower directly outside the Electric Town exit, ten floors of tenants mostly running 10:00-20:00 with a few later. Figures, trading cards, models and the Kotobukiya and Volks floors. This is the building that has been in half the anime set in Akihabara, which is its own reason to go up it

items.title: GiGO Akihabara Building 3
items.notes: Open 10:00-23:30 daily. Floors of UFO catchers, rhythm games and retro cabinets — bring a stack of 100-yen coins and expect the crane machines to be winnable but calibrated. Worth noting for later: the arcades are the most reliable Akihabara category across Jan 1-3, when the shops upstairs each make their own call about opening

items.title: Gyukatsu Motomura Shinjuku Honten
items.notes: Twenty minutes back on the Chuo-Sobu line. Beef cutlet fried rare and served with a hot stone at each seat so you finish your own slices to taste — 11:00-22:00 with last order 21:00, no reservations, and the queue is shortest either side of the dinner rush. Two minutes from the hotel door

items.title: Zero Tokyo
items.notes: A Kabukicho room deliberately rotated against the one from Sunday so the Shinjuku nights are not the same floor five times. Open-format. It is a Tuesday, so check the listing before walking over; the point of being based here is that a wrong call costs a five-minute walk rather than a taxi

items.title: Shibuya Crossing
items.notes: Up to three thousand people cross at once when the lights change. Ground level first from the Hachiko exit, then the second-floor windows over the scramble for the overhead frame that does not need a ticket. Worth knowing now rather than tomorrow: from the morning of Dec 31 the Hachiko statue is fenced off, there is a public drinking ban in force here, the shops near the station suspend alcohol sales and the crossing's big screens go dark at 23:00

items.title: Takeshita-dori, Harajuku
items.notes: One stop north on the Yamanote. Four hundred metres of teen fashion, crepe stands and pop-up character shops, most of it 10:00-20:00 — narrow enough that it is shoulder to shoulder by midday and that is the experience rather than a problem. Omotesando runs parallel one block south if anyone wants the opposite of this

items.title: Lunch at Uobei Shibuya Dogenzaka
items.notes: Back two minutes on the Yamanote. Conveyor sushi at 150 yen a plate ordered from an individual touch panel and delivered along a track at speed — no chef, no queue-jumping, and three adjacent seats is the normal case here rather than the exception, which is not true of most of the food on this trip. 11:00-23:00 on a weekday, last order 22:30

items.title: Starbucks Reserve Roastery Tokyo
items.notes: Three minutes down the Toyoko line to Nakameguro. Four floors on the Meguro river built around a copper cask column that runs the height of the building — the roastery floor at the bottom, the Teavana floor above it, and a cocktail bar at the top. Open 07:00-22:00. It is a coffee shop and it is also the best-built interior on this leg, which is why it earns an hour rather than a takeaway cup

items.title: Shibuya Sky
items.notes: The open-air rooftop deck on top of Shibuya Scramble Square, 10:00-22:30 with last entry 21:20 and twenty-minute entry slots. Booking for today opens at 00:00 JST on 16 Dec, exactly fourteen days ahead, and the sunset slots go within minutes — sunset is 16:35, so the slot to fight for is around 15:40-16:00 and that is the one to be sitting at a screen for. The rooftop closes in wind or rain and only the indoor 46th floor stays open, with no refund for the view, so this is a gamble that pays about four times in five

items.title: Miyashita Park rooftop
items.notes: A park built on the roof of a shopping block, 08:00-23:00 and free — skate bowl, bouldering wall and a lawn looking back at the towers you were just on top of. Five minutes from Shibuya Station and the way in to the alley underneath it

items.title: Shibuya Yokocho
items.notes: Nineteen-odd regional-food counters filling the ground floor under the rooftop park, one prefecture each — Hokkaido crab at one end, Okinawan awamori at the other. It runs 11:00-05:00 Monday to Saturday, so a Wednesday is a late one, and it is the only proper sit-down food near the Shibuya clubs still going at four in the morning. Note the Sunday exception for later in the trip: it closes at 23:00 then instead

items.title: Shibuya standing bars
items.notes: The tachinomi counters in the backstreets off the east exit — beer from about 200 yen, highballs from 300, standing room only and nobody sitting on a seat charge. An hour and a half here costs what one Golden Gai cover costs, and it is where Shibuya actually drinks before midnight

items.title: Harlem
items.notes: The Tokyo hip-hop institution, running in Maruyamacho since 1997 — main room upstairs, smaller bar level below, and the floor does not fill until after midnight. Doors 22:00-23:00, sets to about 05:00, door typically 1,000-3,500 yen with a drink, and confirmed still operating in 2026. The honest caveat is that the calendar is weighted to Friday and Saturday and this is a Wednesday, so read tonight's event before committing the night to it. Ichiran on the far side of the station runs 24 hours and is the walk home

items.title: Slow start in Kabukicho
items.notes: Tonight runs to four or five in the morning, so the daytime is deliberately empty. Two jobs: draw cash if it was not done on the 29th, because the banks and most ATMs are shut from today to Jan 3 and only the convenience-store machines keep working, and check that the countdown ticket is actually in a phone rather than an email nobody has opened

items.title: Gyukatsu Motomura Shinjuku Honten
items.notes: A proper meal before a long night rather than after it. 11:00-22:00, last order 21:00, no reservations — the mid-afternoon gap between the lunch and dinner queues is the easiest time of day to get three seats together here

items.title: Rest before the night
items.notes: Worth knowing before anyone plans a route home: some JR lines including the Yamanote run all night tonight on a reduced timetable, but the Metro and the private lines do not — they run late, to roughly 02:00-03:00, and then stop. Being based at Shinjuku, on the Yamanote, is the advantage here, and it is why the night does not need a taxi plan

items.title: Projection mapping in Nishi-Shinjuku
items.notes: The free nightly show on the Metropolitan Government No. 1 Building wall, twenty minutes on foot from the hotel — the 17:30 screening tonight, before the countdown crowd builds on the same plaza from about 22:00. The observation decks inside are shut today and stay shut through Dec 31

items.title: New Year's Eve dinner at Omoide Yokocho
items.notes: Yakitori and a beer standing up under the tracks. The honest warning is that every stall here sets its own year-end break and a good share shut Dec 31 to Jan 3 without publishing it, so walk the lane and take what has its shutter up rather than aiming at one counter. Ramen Nagi in Golden Gai runs 24 hours and is three minutes away if the whole alley has gone dark

items.title: Countdown at WARP Shinjuku
items.notes: The ticketed club countdown is the real midnight product in Tokyo and it has to be bought in the first half of December. On the 2026 turn a comparable room ran 22:30-04:30 with advance at 6,000 yen sold out before the night, door at 8,000 before 01:00 and 5,000 after — and it stated that if advance sold out there would be no door sales at all before 01:00. Missing the advance window means not getting in until one in the morning. Two things this plan will not do: Club Camelot, which older lists still name for this night, ended nightclub operations on 5 May 2025 and the space is now a rental studio; and the Shibuya street countdown has been cancelled six years running and should be treated as a place you can end up rather than an event. The free fallback is the official Metropolitan Government countdown on the plaza walked past at 17:30 — projection mapping and live performance from about 22:00 to midnight, twenty minutes from this door, with registration opening in the second week of November

items.title: Hanazono Shrine hatsumode on the way home
items.notes: Five minutes from Kabukicho and directly on the walk back from the club. The grounds are open around the clock and the shrine runs a full hatsumode with food stalls through Jan 1-3, at a fraction of the effort of Meiji Jingu — and coming off the floor at half four is the one hour it is genuinely quiet, because the queue only builds from about nine. The other reason this is the plan: Meiji Jingu takes roughly three million people over these three days and, for a group that has been out until four, an hour in a marshalled queue is not the New Year anyone wants

items.title: Late start
items.notes: Nothing before this is worth setting an alarm for. Almost every department store and mall in Tokyo is shut today — Scramble Square, Parco and so the Pokemon Center with it, 109, Isetan, Takashimaya, Ginza Six, Marui, Roppongi Hills, Tokyo Midtown — and several stay shut on Jan 2 as well

items.title: Tokyo National Museum
items.notes: Twenty-five minutes on the Yamanote to Ueno. This is the New Year's Day answer: the museum is closed Dec 26-31 and reopens today, which makes it one of the very few serious things open. On the previous turn the Jan 1 opening ran from 13:00 rather than the usual 09:30, so do not turn up early. 1,000 yen adult, closed Mondays, and open to 20:00 on Fridays and Saturdays. The Honkan's Japanese galleries and the Heiseikan archaeology rooms are the two hours; the Gallery of Horyuji Treasures is the third if there is appetite

items.title: Metropolitan Government South observation deck
items.notes: Back to Shinjuku, twenty-five minutes. Today is the only date in the whole Dec 29 to Jan 3 stretch the decks open, and only the South one — normal daytime entry is free and walk-up, and the deck runs to 22:00 with last entry 21:30. The first-sunrise opening this morning was a lottery rather than a queue, so nothing was missed by sleeping. Sunset was 16:38, so this is the city lit rather than the sunset, and on a clear January evening Fuji sits on the western horizon from up here

items.title: Sushi Zanmai Honten
items.notes: Twenty-five minutes back down to Tsukiji, and worth the trip on exactly this date: it is open 24 hours every day of the year, including today, when most of the city is not. The outer market around it is a different story — it shut on Dec 30 and does not reopen until Jan 5 — so the lanes will be dead and the restaurant will not be. No reservations, and three at the counter is normal here

items.title: Big Echo Shibuya Center-Gai
items.notes: The guaranteed-open plan on the one night when Golden Gai's bars each make their own call and none of them publish it. Twenty-four-hour karaoke at roughly 225-1,985 yen a head depending on the hour, private room, drinks ordered in. The clubs that ran countdowns last night are either shut or empty tonight, and pretending otherwise would waste the evening. Ichiran on Center-Gai runs 24 hours for the walk back

items.title: Meiji Jingu hatsumode
items.notes: Five minutes on the Yamanote to Harajuku. Roughly three million people come through here over Jan 1-3, and the peak windows are 22:00 to 03:00 and from 10:00 onwards each day — so 08:00 to 09:30 is the one civilised slot in the whole period and it is the reason for the early start. The approach is a wide gravel avenue through 70 hectares of planted forest, every tree of it donated and hand-planted in the 1920s, which is the part most people walk straight past

items.title: animate Ikebukuro Main Store
items.notes: Fifteen minutes north on the Yamanote. Today is hatsu-uri, the first sale of the year and the day the lucky bags go out, and this is animate's busiest day of the year — queues form before the 10:00 opening and stores often open early when the line is long, so arriving at ten means arriving behind it. Nine floors, one genre per floor. If there is one bag to queue for on this trip, it is here rather than at a department store

items.title: Pokemon Center MEGA TOKYO
items.notes: In Sunshine City, ten minutes east on foot. Back to normal 10:00-20:00 hours today after the New Year closure — the Parco branch in Shibuya was shut yesterday and this one is the reason the Pokemon stop is on Jan 2 rather than Jan 1. The Pikachu Sweets cafe and the trading-card counter are on the same floor

items.title: Lunch in Sunshine City
items.notes: Eat in the building rather than going back out — most Ikebukuro independents are still on a New Year break and the mall floors are open and full. Sunshine City runs its own lucky bags today too, on the way through

items.title: Ginza Six
items.notes: Twenty minutes on the Marunouchi line. Shops 10:30-20:30, and Ginza's stores reopen today with their own lucky bags after being shut for New Year's Day. The rooftop garden is free, runs 07:00-23:00 and is one of the few open spaces in Ginza with somewhere to sit; the Tsutaya bookshop on the sixth floor is the other reason to come in rather than walk past

items.title: Marunouchi Naka-dori illumination
items.notes: A ten-minute walk north. Champagne-gold lights strung through 1.2 km of zelkova trees between Yurakucho and Otemachi, lit 16:00-23:00 with the season running mid-November to mid-February — which is the point: this covers the whole stay, whereas the Roppongi Keyakizaka lights that most guides send you to finish on Dec 25, two days before the party reaches Tokyo. The separate avenue section and the pedestrian street closures also ended Dec 25, so the road is live traffic now — shoot from the pavement

items.title: Vampire Cafe
items.notes: Seventh floor of a Ginza block, ten minutes back south. Coffin tables, a fake-blood fountain and staff in full costume — one of the longest-running themed restaurants in Tokyo, and a novelty stop rather than a meal anyone would order for the food. Reserve, because it is small and it is the New Year week

items.title: Sel Octagon Tokyo
items.notes: Six minutes on the Hibiya line to Roppongi. A large basement room on Gaien-Higashi-dori built around a lighting rig closer to a festival stage than a bar, roughly 22:00-04:30 — and the Roppongi club that is not fed by touts on the street, which is the reason it is the pick here rather than anything on the strip. Saturday is one of only three weekend club nights on the whole Tokyo leg, the others being New Year's Eve and Jan 8, so this is one of three chances at a real floor. Door prices are per head and a trio is a target: buy at the door of the room itself and walk past anyone offering a deal on the pavement

items.title: Shinjuku → Mitaka
items.notes: Twenty minutes on the Chuo Rapid, then the museum shuttle from the south exit or a fifteen-minute walk along the Tamagawa Josui canal path. Today is the national return-travel peak and the worst single day of the year on the rails, so the whole day is deliberately built on one line in western Tokyo — Mitaka and Nakano are both on the Chuo and neither goes near a Shinkansen platform. The Kamakura day was moved off today for the same reason: the Enoden is overloaded through Jan 1-3 with boarding queues at Kamakura Station running forty minutes. The Koenji and Shimokitazawa vintage plan came off too — independent second-hand shops are exactly the category that stays shut through Jan 3, tenant by tenant, with nothing published in advance

items.title: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
items.notes: Advance reservation only, no door sales, and the tickets for the whole of January were released at 10:00 JST on 10 Dec — that is 06:15 in Kathmandu, and they routinely go the same morning, so somebody had to be awake for it. There is no second chance and no walk-up. Open 10:00-18:00 with entry slots at 10:00, 12:00, 14:00 and 16:00; closed Tuesdays, and the annual winter closure runs on the Dec 27 to Jan 2 pattern, which leaves Jan 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 as the only possible dates on this trip. 1,000 yen. No photography inside — that is enforced, not advisory — and the short film in the basement theatre changes monthly and is only ever shown here

items.title: Lunch in Kichijoji
items.notes: One stop back down the Chuo line and the obvious stop between the museum and Nakano. Pick from what actually has its shutter up rather than from a name chosen in advance — Jan 3 is the day independent shops each make their own call, and the arcade around the station is where enough of them will be open to make that work

items.title: Nakano Broadway
items.notes: Twelve minutes east on the Chuo line, then a five-minute arcade walk from the north exit. A 1966 shopping complex that turned into the collectors' building — 10:00-20:00 for the building, but most of the collector shops only open at 12:00. It is open on a Sunday and individual shops still set their own New Year closures; the chain publishes a year-end operating page each December, so read that rather than assuming. This is a confirm day, not a certainty

items.title: Mandarake Nakano
items.notes: More than twenty separate shops spread across the upper floors of the same building, each one a single specialism — cels, vintage Showa-era figures, doujinshi, first-run Jump, model kits — which is the difference between here and the single eight-floor Akihabara complex. 12:00-20:00 daily. This is where the rare Dragon Ball and One Piece pieces actually are, and the prices reflect that

items.title: Sugoi Niboshi Ramen Nagi, Golden Gai
items.notes: Five minutes back into Shinjuku on the Chuo line. Up a near-vertical staircase in the Golden Gai main building — a heavy dried-sardine broth that people either love or find too much, which is the point of it. Advertised as 24 hours year-round, but it is a small owner-run shop and can still take a short year-end break, so look at the door rather than promising it to anyone

items.title: Whiska
items.notes: A whisky bar in Golden Gai with a jazz-CD soundtrack, and a different door from the one on the 27th — the whole point of a two-hundred-bar alley is not to go back to the same five seats. Assume half the lane is dark tonight and pick from what has its light on; the seat charge is per person and posted at the door

items.title: Shinjuku → Kamakura
items.notes: Sixty-one minutes direct on the Shonan-Shinjuku Line for about 920 yen, no transfer. Today is the first day clear of the Jan 1-3 hatsumode crush that had boarding queues at Kamakura Station running forty minutes, and clear of the return-travel peak that made yesterday unusable for anything with a long train on it

items.title: Kotoku-in, the Great Buddha of Kamakura
items.notes: Five minutes on the Enoden from Kamakura to Hase, then a seven-minute walk. An 11.4 m bronze Amida cast in 1252, sitting in the open since the hall around it was destroyed by a tsunami in the fifteenth century. 08:00-17:00 October to March with entry until 16:45, no closing days, 300 yen — and for another 50 yen you can go inside the statue and see the casting seams from the back, which takes five minutes and is the part nobody photographs

items.title: Kamakurakokomae Station crossing
items.notes: Four stops further along the single-track Enoden. The level crossing from the opening sequence of Slam Dunk, where the road meets the sea wall with Enoshima on the horizon — a straight hit on the anime side of this trip and it costs nothing but the fare. It is a working level crossing on a residential street and Kamakura City has put up signage about people standing in the road for the shot: take it from the pavement and let the train come to the frame

items.title: Lunch on Komachi-dori
items.notes: Back into Kamakura on the Enoden. The covered shopping street running north from the station towards Tsurugaoka Hachimangu — shirasu on rice, croquettes and purple sweet-potato soft serve eaten walking. Everything here is open again now that the hatsumode week has broken, which was not true yesterday

items.title: Kamakura → Yokohama Minatomirai
items.notes: JR Yokosuka line to Yokohama, about 25 minutes, then the Minatomirai line two stops to Bashamichi. The museum is five minutes on foot from the exit

items.title: CUPNOODLES MUSEUM Yokohama
items.notes: Verify this one before relying on it. Beyond its normal Dec 31 to Jan 1 closure, this museum was shut for the whole of January 2026 for works, and the sister site in Osaka ran its own year-end maintenance the same winter — whether that repeats in 2027 was unknown when this was written, so check the official site.
