Assuming it is open: 10:00-18:00, last entry 17:00, closed Tuesdays, so a Monday works. 500 yen entry plus 500 yen a cup at My CUPNOODLES Factory, where you decorate a blank cup, pick a soup and four toppings and watch it sealed and shrink-wrapped. That is a forty-five-minute activity the group will still be talking about later. The cup factory is same-day but takes a numbered ticket that can run out on a busy afternoon; the Chicken Ramen Factory needs booking ahead

items.title: Yokohama Chinatown
items.notes: One stop on the Minatomirai line to Motomachi-Chukagai. The largest Chinatown in Japan — about three hundred restaurants and stalls in a ten-block grid behind painted gates, with street counters selling steamed buns, xiaolongbao and grilled skewers to eat standing. It is dark by 16:45 and the lanterns are lit, which is why this is the evening half. Worth filing: it is one of the very few food districts near Tokyo that stays busy right through Jan 1-3, so it is the answer if the New Year dinner problem in Shinjuku ever bites

items.title: Yokohama → Shinjuku
items.notes: About fifty-five minutes back, Minatomirai line to Yokohama then the Shonan-Shinjuku or Tokyu-Fukutoshin through service

items.title: Bar Shinjuku Whisky Salon
items.notes: A quiet bar next to Golden Gai, run by one of the country's named whisky specialists, with a list deep enough to make the choice the entertainment. A Monday in Roppongi is the worst combination of a dead floor and active touts, and after twelve hours out on trains this is the honest end to the day rather than a club nobody wants to be in

items.title: Shinjuku → Toshimaen
items.notes: Toei Oedo line direct from Shinjuku, about 25 minutes, then a short walk. Allow the extra — the entry slot is timed and there is no re-entry once inside

items.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour Tokyo
items.notes: Timed entry, non-refundable, and January is peak — 6,600 to 7,300 yen adult depending on the date. Tickets are also sold at the onsite ticket office, contrary to the common claim that it is website-only, but pre-booking is the only sane approach in the New Year week and this should have gone in as the calendar opened. No re-entry, and four hours is the minimum rather than the comfortable case. The Ghibli Museum is usually named as the fallback if this sells out: it closes on Tuesdays and today is a Tuesday, so it is not one — teamLab, Nakano or an anime-cafe day would be

items.title: Nerima → Shibakoen
items.notes: Oedo line the whole way round to Akabanebashi, about 35 minutes, and the tower is five minutes from that exit

items.title: Tokyo Tower
items.notes: Main deck 09:00-22:30 with last entry 22:00, 1,500 yen; the Top Deck at 250 m is a separate timed tour worth booking online. Sunset is 16:41, so a late-afternoon arrival buys the last of the daylight and the lights coming on from one ticket. Winter nights give the sharpest panoramas of the year here, and the glass floor panels on the main deck are the thing people either love or refuse to stand on

items.title: Tokyo Midtown Walkway of Light
items.notes: A fifteen-minute walk from the tower, or one stop on the Oedo line. The Walkway of Light runs 17:00-23:00 and on the annual pattern stays lit into late February, so unlike the Roppongi Keyakizaka lights it is still on. Shops 11:00-21:00, restaurants to 23:00, and the outdoor rink beside it is shut on Jan 1 only

items.title: Dinner at Tokyo Midtown
items.notes: Restaurants in the building run to 23:00, which makes this the simplest sit-down within a two-minute walk of the lights. Everything around Roppongi Crossing at this hour is priced for the club crowd and staffed for it too

items.title: Karaoke Kan, Shibuya
items.notes: The karaoke box used in Lost in Translation — rooms 601 and 602 are the ones, and they can be asked for. Fifteen minutes from Roppongi. The night moves out of Roppongi on purpose: the good room there programmes Friday and Saturday, and a Tuesday on that strip is a quiet floor with active touts on the pavement outside it

items.title: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
items.notes: 09:00-16:30 from Oct 1 to Mar 14, last entry 16:00, 500 yen, closed Mondays — and closed Dec 29 to Jan 3 every year on top of that, which leaves Jan 5 to Jan 8 as the only four dates on this whole trip when it is open, and three of those are already spoken for. Ten minutes on foot from Kabukicho. Fifty-eight hectares holding a French formal garden, an English landscape garden and a Japanese one side by side, the greenhouse, and a Taiwanese pavilion on the pond

items.title: Shinjuku → Toyosu
items.notes: Marunouchi line to Ginza, Yurakucho line east to Toyosu, about forty minutes. The whole afternoon runs east from here on one line, which is why the garden had to be the morning

items.title: teamLab Planets TOKYO
items.notes: Open 09:00-22:00 with last entry 21:00, from 3,600 yen, timed entry and January is peak — book as the calendar opens. One warning that is not on the ticket page: it closes for maintenance on scattered single weekdays that are only published on its own calendar, so check this specific date before booking anything around it. Practical matter — you walk barefoot through knee-deep water and the floors are mirrored, so trousers that roll above the knee, and a skirt is a bad idea. Phones survive it but bags do not; there are lockers

items.title: Monja Street, Tsukishima
items.notes: Two stops back west on the Yurakucho line, four minutes. About eighty monja shops along Nishinaka-dori, and the way it works is that shops take names at the door rather than reservations — so the plan is to walk the street, put a name down at the one you want, and spend the wait on the rest of the lane. The whole street closes for several days over New Year, generally Dec 31 to Jan 3, so today is safely on the right side of it

items.title: Monja Kondo Honten
items.notes: Roughly 17:00-22:00 on a weekday. Monjayaki is cooked on the hotplate in front of you and eaten off the plate with a small metal spatula, scraped in crisp patches rather than served — it looks wrong and it is correct. Two or three monja between three people is the right order, not one each. Cash is safest along this street

items.title: Ebisu Yokocho
items.notes: Thirty minutes west. About twenty open-fronted izakaya counters filling the ground floor of an old shopping arcade a few minutes from Ebisu Station, dressed to look like a post-war market — shared tables, an aisle one person wide, and it runs 17:00-05:00. A real izakaya night rather than a chain, and late enough to be the last stop instead of the first. Several stalls close Jan 1-3 but today is clear of that

items.title: Shinjuku → Shimo-Yoshida on the Fuji Excursion
items.notes: The train is the whole problem with this day. About four round trips a day, 1h53 to 1h58, around 4,130 yen, every seat reserved with no non-reserved cars at all, and it sells out — the seats went on sale at 10:00 JST one month before, so 7 Dec 2026, which is 06:15 in Kathmandu. The first train leaves at 07:30 and reaches Kawaguchiko at 09:28; get off one stop early at Shimo-Yoshida, which puts the pagoda fifteen minutes away on foot instead of a bus ride back. Highway buses from the Shinjuku terminal are the fallback at about two hours and 2,200 yen, two an hour, but they sit in New Year road congestion Dec 29-31 and Jan 2-4 — Jan 7 is clear of both, which is part of why the day is here

items.title: Chureito Pagoda, Arakurayama Sengen Park
items.notes: Fifteen minutes on foot from the station to the shrine at the bottom, then 398 steps up to the viewing terrace. Free and open at all times. The composition is fixed by a purpose-built deck, so everyone shoots the same frame and the only variables are the air and the queue for the middle of the rail — December and early January have the driest, clearest air of the year, which is the actual reason this day sits in January rather than being wished for earlier. The steps are unlit: nobody should still be up there after 16:30, which is what caps the afternoon at the other end of the lake

items.title: Shimo-Yoshida → Kawaguchiko
items.notes: One stop on the Fujikyuko line, then the station is the hub for the sightseeing buses. The two-day sightseeing bus pass is about 1,500 yen and pays for itself on the Oishi Park round trip alone

items.title: Lunch at Kawaguchiko Station
items.notes: Hoto — flat wheat noodles simmered in miso with pumpkin and root vegetables — is the Yamanashi dish and the station block is where the shops are. Eat before the bus rather than at the lake: Oishi Park is a strip of shoreline with a shop, not a place to sit down for an hour

items.title: Oishi Park, Lake Kawaguchi
items.notes: About twenty-five minutes on the retro-bus loop from the station, free to enter. The north shore looks straight across the water at Fuji with the flower beds in front — bare in winter, which is honestly better, because nothing competes with the mountain. Two frames from one day and both completely different from the pagoda. Straight is that the mirror reflection everyone photographs needs a still morning and this is an afternoon: what the afternoon gives instead is direct light on the south face. If the reflection is the priority, run the day the other way round and take the pagoda after lunch — but then the unlit steps become the problem

items.title: Kawaguchiko Station before the train
items.notes: Back on the bus with time in hand. Sunset at the lake is 16:47 and the last direct return leaves at 17:38 — miss it and the alternative is a bus in the dark, so the buffer is deliberate

items.title: Kawaguchiko → Shinjuku
items.notes: The last direct Fuji Excursion of the day, arriving Shinjuku at 19:27. Reserved, same as the morning leg, and booked in the same transaction

items.title: Fuunji
items.notes: Eight minutes south of Shinjuku Station on foot, so it is genuinely on the way back from the platform. The tsukemen here is the famous one — thick noodles dipped into a dense chicken-and-fish broth. Open 11:00-15:00 and 17:00-21:00, closed Sundays plus a New Year break, and a Thursday works. About ten counter seats plus standing, so three people will be split up and there will be a queue: this is a twenty-minute meal, not a sit-down

items.title: Zoetrope Whisky Bar
items.notes: More than two hundred Japanese whiskies in a tiny cinema-themed room off the west side of Shinjuku, with silent films projected on the wall behind the bar. A short quiet night on purpose — tomorrow is a park from nine in the morning and then the last club night of the trip after it

items.title: Shinjuku → Maihama
items.notes: Chuo Rapid to Tokyo Station, then the Keyo line to Maihama — allow for the long underground walk between the two platforms at Tokyo, which is a genuine ten minutes and catches people out. About fifty-five minutes door to gate

items.title: Tokyo DisneySea
items.notes: Typically 09:00-21:00, but the daily calendar for a month is only published around the 8th of the previous month, so the hours for today only appeared in early December — check them rather than assuming. Tickets were released at 14:00 JST on 8 Nov 2026, the same date two months out; date-specific, one park, and there is no park hopper. Jan 8 sits inside the New Year special-event window that runs Jan 1-11 and outside the Dec 26-31 gap week, which has peak crowds and no seasonal programme — that is why the park day is here and not earlier, and it should not be moved. Fantasy Springs and Journey to the Center of the Earth are the two to get standby passes for first

items.title: Maihama → Shibuya
items.notes: About fifty minutes. Out of the park a little before close rather than with everyone else — the Maihama platform after a park closing is its own event

items.title: Ichiran Shibuya
items.notes: Twenty-four hours. Order from the machine, fill in the paper form for firmness, richness and the red sauce, and eat in a booth facing a bamboo blind. One thing worth knowing with three people: Ichiran seats you in individual booths by design, and the dividers have to be folded back on request — which is not guaranteed at peak, so ask on the way in rather than after sitting down

items.title: Harlem — the last club night
items.notes: Friday, and the last of only three weekend club nights on the Tokyo leg. Doors 22:00-23:00, sets to about 05:00, door typically 1,000-3,500 yen with a drink, and the floor does not fill until after midnight — which is the second wind of a fourteen-hour day and worth knowing before anyone promises to make it. Shibuya Yokocho under Miyashita Park serves until 05:00 and is the only proper sit-down food near these clubs still going at four

items.title: Slow final breakfast
items.notes: Unhurried last morning after the final night out. The flight is not until 17:35, so the whole morning is genuinely free and nothing needs to be rushed

items.title: Check out of the Kabukicho hotel
items.notes: Real booked checkout is 10:00. The desk will hold the bags for the morning, which is what makes a last shopping run possible at all

items.title: Last shopping run in Shinjuku
items.notes: A Saturday morning, and Jan 9 is not the day to discover that the one shop somebody saved for last opens at 11:00 — check before walking to it. Keep the tax-free paperwork and everything bought under it together and out of the suitcases; it has to go through the airport, not into the hold

items.title: Transfer to Haneda (HND)
items.notes: Tokyo/Shinjuku to Haneda by train or airport limousine bus; allow ~3h before the international departure and check in for the flight home. Japan refunds consumption tax at the departure airport rather than at the shop, so keep anything you bought and its receipts in hand luggage, not checked, and leave extra time for the refund counter before check-in
